heading: INT. TIDE-CLOCK TOWER - INSIDE A WHALE SKELETON - DUSK

units.text: INT. TIDE-CLOCK TOWER - INSIDE A WHALE SKELETON - DUSK
A cathedral of bone.
Ribs arch overhead like the hull of an overturned ship, strung with lanterns and rope ladders.
At the center, a vast brass clock whose pendulum is a swinging glass bell filled with seawater.
Each tick sloshes a silver tide across the floor.
BRAMWELL TOLLIVER, 70s, tiny and bent, in a coat patched with sailcloth, oils a gear with a feather.
A brass monocle sits on his nose, one lens fogged.
The great doors boom open.
LADY SERAPHINE VANE, 40s, strides in, sea-green cloak dragging a wake of damp, silver rings on every finger.
Behind her trots PIP, a clockwork heron, tall as a child, copper beak clicking.
You're late, Lady Vane. The tide has turned twice.
units.name: BRAMWELL

units.text: The tide turns when I command it, Bramwell.
units.name: SERAPHINE

units.text: Not in my tower.
units.name: BRAMWELL

units.text: Pip tips her head and clicks.
Seraphine sets a gloved hand on the heron's neck, and the clicking softens.
Pip, quiet. He is an old man and he is frightened.
units.name: SERAPHINE

units.text: I am not frightened. I am furious.
units.name: BRAMWELL

units.text: Furious is frightened wearing boots.
units.name: PIP

units.text: Bramwell laughs despite himself, a dry bark.
The pendulum swings.
A silver tide washes over their feet and recedes.
I have come to take the Moonweight, Bramwell.
units.name: SERAPHINE

units.text: The Moonweight holds the tide in its place.
units.name: BRAMWELL

units.text: The tide has held long enough. The sea is tired of being told when to rise.
units.name: SERAPHINE

units.text: And when it rises with no hand upon it? What then, Lady?
units.name: BRAMWELL

units.text: Then it rises. And we float.
units.name: SERAPHINE

units.text: Bramwell lays the feather down on the gear.
He crosses to a small iron door in a rib, thumbs a latch, and takes out a lead-grey disc the size of a dinner plate.
It hums.
Forty years I tended this. My wife is buried under that floor.
units.name: BRAMWELL

units.text: I know.
units.name: SERAPHINE

units.text: You know. And still you ask.
units.name: BRAMWELL

units.text: I do not ask, Bramwell. I came out of courtesy.
units.name: SERAPHINE

units.text: Courtesy is a polite word for a knife.
units.name: PIP

units.text: Pip.
units.name: SERAPHINE

units.text: I only quote.
units.name: PIP

units.text: Bramwell weighs the disc in both hands.
The pendulum bell slows.
A lantern gutters.
Somewhere high in the ribs, a gull cries.
You were a girl when you first came up those stairs. Do you remember what you asked me?
units.name: BRAMWELL

units.text: I asked if the whale was still alive.
units.name: SERAPHINE

units.text: And I said?
units.name: BRAMWELL

units.text: That it was only sleeping.
units.name: SERAPHINE

units.text: Was I lying?
units.name: BRAMWELL

units.text: No.
units.name: SERAPHINE

units.text: She holds out both hands.
Bramwell looks at the Moonweight, then at her, and his shoulders drop.
Take it. Let the sea wake what it must.
units.name: BRAMWELL

units.text: Seraphine receives the disc.
Its hum deepens.
The silver tide climbs slowly up the ribs, quieter now, and the great bell comes to rest.
Is that the last tick?
units.name: PIP

units.text: For tonight, small one. For tonight.
units.name: BRAMWELL

units.text: Seraphine bows her head.
The lanterns dim one by one.
